Patch on top of [v2.2](../../releases/tag/v2.2). One field-reported fix, no
change to charge behaviour.

Personal fork, developed and tested on one machine with one powder. It dispenses
gunpowder charges for ammunition reloading - verify weights independently.

| File | Board | |
|---|---|---|
| `opentrickler-v2.21-pico2_w.uf2` | Raspberry Pi Pico **2** W (RP2350) | developed and tested on this |
| `opentrickler-v2.21-pico_w.uf2` | Raspberry Pi Pico W (RP2040) | boot fix from v2.2, still unconfirmed |

**No EEPROM change** - settings and profiles carry over, no need to re-run Learn
Powder.

## "No flow, check tube" on a tube that was flowing

Reported with a photo: Learn Powder aborts with **No flow, check tube** while the
fine motor is visibly running and dispensing, the scale reading **0.22 gr**.

The tube was fine. The check was wrong.

Learn aborted when a calibration throw measured below a minimum flow *rate*
(0.02 gr/s). Flow is mass divided by run time, so the mass that floor demands
grows with how long the step runs - and the fine ladder's slowest step runs for
up to 12 seconds:

| step | run | mass it demanded |
|---|---|---|
| coarse probe | 1.0 s | 0.02 gr |
| fine probe | 4.0 s | 0.08 gr |
| **fine ladder, slowest** | **12.0 s** | **0.24 gr** |

So it required 0.24 gr from the step deliberately chosen to be the slowest the
tube can manage, and 0.22 gr missed by two hundredths of a grain. The threshold
was strictest exactly where the firmware asks the tube to go slowest, which is
backwards. A slower fine tube - a different tube, or a denser powder - hits it
where a faster one never will.

Now judged on **how much powder actually landed**, not the rate: under 0.05 gr
off a whole timed run means nothing is coming out. A slow throw is a perfectly
usable data point for the fit; only an empty tube is not, and an empty tube
delivers nothing at any speed or duration.

The message also reports what it measured - `No flow: 0.22gr in 12s` - rather
than asserting a diagnosis. "No flow" was simply false, and it sent someone
inspecting hardware that was working.

## Also in v2.2, if you are coming from v2.1

- **Pico W boot failure** - the stepper PIO program was loaded once per motor,
  which RP2040 does not have the instruction memory for once the wifi chip has
  taken its share. Motor error plus a display that never came up, from one
  cause. Fixed, but still not confirmed on RP2040 hardware.
- **Backup and restore** now includes the Learn Powder settings, which Export
  Config had been silently dropping, and the buttons sit under a labelled
  **Backup & Restore** heading instead of unmarked at the foot of the page.
